evals.prompt: My Shopify collection page https://example-store.com/collections/linen-dresses is just a product grid with zero text. Write the SEO content for it and tell me exactly where each block goes on the page.
evals.expected_output: Runs the four phases and delivers the standard five-part deliverable (1. Spec scorecard by ID, 2. Audit findings, 3. Competitor benchmark, 4. Build, 5. Acceptance). Phase 1: scores the page against the COL spec rows plus the common rows C-01 to C-26 linked from skills/seo-geo-audit/references/common-page-spec.md. Phase 2: gives the seo_audit.py and section_audit.py --type collection commands plus a curl raw-HTML check, and maps findings (thin_content, no_bold, no_question_h2, schema_none) to spec IDs. Phase 3: picks 3-5 category URLs of the stores and marketplaces ranking on 'linen dresses', runs page_benchmark.py --type collection, reads the block gaps and below-median metrics, and states the information gain. Phase 4 builds: Search Console query mining first, then a 1-2 sentence intro at the top directly under the H1 opening with the category keyword bolded, and a 400-800 word rich text block placed BELOW the product grid containing H2/H3 headings phrased as buyer questions (how to choose a linen dress, which weave or weight for which season, sizing, care), a comparison table of sub-types, 3-5 definitions of category terms (for example European flax, GSM, garment-washed), an FAQ of 3+ real questions with 40-80 word answers, and internal links to sub-collections plus 2-3 related blog guides, with semantic bolding, 60%+ placement and no term above 2.5%. Explains why the long text goes at the bottom (a top block pushes products below the fold and costs conversions, while a bottom block feeds Google and AI assistants at no sales cost). Includes H1, title, slug and handwritten meta description, product cards with images and prices as text, and CollectionPage, ItemList and BreadcrumbList JSON-LD with no empty nodes, pointing to the seo-schema-markup skill. Ends with the acceptance test (scripts re-run). Placeholders {to confirm} for unverified facts. No em-dashes, no emojis.

evals.prompt: Search Console shows 40,000 'Discovered, currently not indexed' URLs on my store, almost all parameter URLs like /collections/shoes?filter.v.option.color=red&size=9&sort=price. Googlebot is crawling thousands of filter combinations and new products take weeks to index. How do I fix this without losing my 'red running shoes' rankings?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses faceted navigation crawl waste as a Fail on spec row COL-17 (and COL-18 for the facet exception), audited in Phase 2 by running seo_audit.py on the clean collection URL and a filter URL and reading the Search Console page indexing reports. Phase 4 build applies the decision table: rel=canonical from filtered URLs to the clean collection URL as the default, meta robots noindex for filter combinations that are already indexed (kept crawlable until they drop out), and robots.txt Disallow patterns for multi-filter combinations and sort parameters to stop crawl waste, with the explicit warning that robots.txt blocking and noindex cannot work on the same URL at the same time because a blocked page is never fetched so its noindex is never seen (sequence: noindex first, block later). Preserves the exception: a facet like red running shoes stays indexable only if it passes the three tests (real search demand, distinct inventory, unique title/H1/content with self-canonical); Phase 3 benchmarking of the stores ranking on the term can show whether competitors expose that facet as a landing page. Mentions that the Search Console URL Parameters tool was retired in 2022, cites Google's faceted navigation documentation, and points to references/faceted-navigation-playbook.md for the Shopify-specific parameter patterns and the monitoring loop. Delivers in the standard deliverable shape (spec scorecard rows, audit findings, build directives table by URL pattern, acceptance check in Search Console and a re-run of the scripts).

evals.prompt: My SEO plugin canonicalizes page 2 and beyond of every category to page 1 and adds rel=next/prev tags. Products that only appear on pages 3 to 6 are dropping out of Google's index. Is this setup correct?
evals.expected_output: States the setup is wrong (a Fail on spec row COL-19) and explains the mechanism: canonicalizing page 2+ to page 1 declares the paginated pages duplicates, so Google consolidates to page 1 and stops crawling deep pages, and products linked only from page 3+ lose their only crawl path and deindex, which matches the observed symptom. Phase 2 audit: run seo_audit.py on ?page=2 and read canonical_other as the failing finding. Phase 4 build prescribes the fix: self-referencing canonical on every paginated page, unique titles in the form 'Category - Page N | Brand', plain crawlable a-href pagination links (not JS-only buttons, with a paginated fallback for infinite scroll), and keeping page 2+ indexable. Notes that rel=next/prev has not been used by Google for indexing since 2019, so it is harmless but fixes nothing. Cites Google's e-commerce pagination documentation (developers.google.com). Ends with the acceptance test from the deliverable: re-run the script on page 2 and confirm a self-canonical.
